title: AI opens new era in cognitive studies of wild primates
excerpt: Emory anthropologists created an AI system to automate behavioral studies of capuchins monkeys in the wild. The novel method provides a roadmap for the first scalable, systematic way to evaluate and monitor the cognitive abilities of wild primates.
content_html:
“This project builds on the legacy of Frans de Waal,” says Federico Sánchez Vargas, first author of the paper and an Emory PhD student in anthropology.

De Waal pioneered studies of animal cognition as director of Emory’s Living Links Center for the Advanced Study of Ape and Human Evolution, while also writing best-selling books that helped popularize the field. He passed away in 2024.

In addition to lab-based behavioral experiments, de Waal “gave us intimate, beautiful portraits of the lives of primates, treating them as individuals,” Sánchez Vargas says. “Our AI method allows us to more deeply understand individuals that we already have data on through field observation. We can now automate cognitive testing of them and quantify the findings. It’s a way of getting into the minds behind the personalities. Studying individuals in their natural environments, where there are tons of variations in their life experiences, lets us learn how environmental influences shaped them.”

Co-authors of the paper include Jacob Abernethy, Georgia Tech associate professor of computer science; and Sai Rakshith Potluri, a former Georgia Tech graduate research assistant who is now a software engineer at ExtraHop in Seattle.

The open-source paper includes a guide to the computer coding developed for the system, along with a blueprint to build a low-tech, low-cost field-research platform and to integrate all the components into a closed-loop pipeline. The authors hope other scientists will adapt their AI method to generate cognitive data spanning different species of wild primates, living in a range of environments.

Benítez’ work lies at the intersection of anthropology, psychology and evolutionary biology. She studies cooperation and other social behaviors in monkeys, including a captive population of tufted capuchins in a laboratory and wild, white-faced capuchins in the Taboga Forest Reserve of northeastern Costa Rica. She is a co-director of Capuchinos de Taboga, a research project launched in 2017 in collaboration with the Universidad Nacional Técnica of Costa Rica.

Experiments with animals in labs can be tightly controlled. The results, however, may be skewed since the animal is not interacting within its natural environment. Animal behavior experiments in the wild provide valid social and ecological contexts but they are challenging to design and to control.

“I’m trying to bridge that gap,” Benítez says.

She decided to investigate the potential of AI to achieve this aim.

A seed grant from Emory’s AI.Humanity program launched a collaboration between Benítez and Abernethy to design an AI model for facial recognition of wild capuchins.

Abernethy and Potluri used an open-source software known as YOLO (You Only Look Once) to develop a model to run on a laptop. The researchers trained the model on high-quality GoPro imagery of six wild capuchins interacting with testing platforms in Taboga.

Emory and Georgia Tech undergraduate students performed the labor-intensive task of digitally placing “bounding boxes” to frame the faces of the monkeys in thousands of still images and videos tagged with their identities.

The result was a facial-recognition system that could identify these six capuchins with 97% accuracy from static images, video and live footage in the field.

Sánchez Vargas, who joined Emory as a graduate student in 2023, took on the next phase of the AI project: figuring out how to integrate the facial-recognition model into a field-friendly, scalable computer interface that could present tasks to interacting capuchins and dispense food rewards.

“The model was great at identifying six monkeys, but there are 100 capuchins at the Costa Rica field site,” he says. “And we didn’t have high quality video of all of these individuals, which is needed to train the model.”

Sánchez Vargas’ undergraduate degrees are in evolutionary biology and psychology. He is not an expert computer coder, but he dove into the challenge, using Python programming language to simplify and change the parameters of the original facial-recognition model.

“I essentially dumbed it down,” he says, so that instead of classifying individual capuchin faces, the system recognized any capuchin monkey — and only capuchins.

The idea, he explains, was to enable the system to trigger a webcam to record video whenever a capuchin approached a computer touchscreen, rapidly generating a larger, more up-to-date dataset of faces from the interacting monkeys. The resulting videos could then be used to keep training the facial-recognition model, expanding its face-recognition repertoire.

A second Python script Sánchez Vargas developed uses a program called “pygame” to facilitate interactive stimuli for use in games or cognitive testing. The researchers created a simple stimulus to habituate the monkeys to the system: a blue square covering the computer touchscreen that records when a capuchin touches it. At the monkey’s touch, the script signals a motor circuit to dispense a food reward.

The two Python scripts are integrated to run simultaneously on a Raspberry Pi, a tiny computer about half the size of an iPhone. The entire system can run for eight hours on a lightweight battery pack before it needs recharging.

“It was important to us that our technology be both low cost and ecologically friendly,” Sánchez Vargas says. 

The next challenge was to create a wildlife-proof, weather-proof platform to house all the components of the system.

“We built it in my garage,” Benítez says.

She and Sánchez Vargas bought planks of pine, deck sealant, rubber insulating strips and plastic piping from Home Depot.

“A person helping us asked, ‘What is the project you’re working on?’” Benítez says. “We didn’t go into it; it would have been a bit complicated to explain.”

Emory TechLab helped Sánchez Vargas create a 3D printed, plastic food dispenser.

The two researchers put together a wooden box, only about 20 inches tall, to house the system’s components: a webcam, a computer touchscreen, the Raspberry Pi, the food dispenser and a rotary motor to power the dispenser. 

“It was a lot of work but also a lot of fun,” Sánchez Vargas says. “One of the best parts of working in animal cognition is getting creative, trying to put yourself into the mind of the animal you’re studying, so you can develop a good way to engage them in experiments.”

Finally, it was time to test their creation in the field.

Upon arriving at the Capuchinos de Toboga facility in Costa Rica, Sánchez Vargas remembers feeling a few last-minute jitters. Would the prototype function as envisioned?

“We had to get up super early, at four in the morning,” he says, “and drive a long way down this bumpy road to get to the research site.”

The team secured the CapuchinAI box to a platform, loaded its food dispenser with dried slices of forest banana, and waited nearby.

“For the first couple of days that we did this, no capuchins visited,” Sánchez Vargas says. “I was beginning to worry.”   

The third day, however, a large male capuchin named Trompudo, which means “big snout,” could not resist the scent of banana.

“He climbs on the box and starts slapping the back of it,” Sánchez Vargas recalls. “Finally, he slaps the touchscreen and a banana slice pops out.”

Trompudo gobbled up the food then put his hand on the screen again. Another banana slice popped out.

“It was almost like you could see him realizing, ‘Ah, that’s what you have to do, touch the screen!’” Sánchez Vargas says. “It was amazing to watch an individual learn something so quickly.”

blocks.html_en: A seed grant from Emory’s AI.Humanity program launched a collaboration between Benítez and Abernethy to design an AI model for facial recognition of wild capuchins.

sentences.en: A seed grant from Emory’s AI.Humanity program launched a collaboration between Benítez and Abernethy to design an AI model for facial recognition of wild capuchins.
sentences.zh: 埃默里大学 AI.Humanity 项目的种子基金启动了贝尼特斯和阿伯内西之间的合作，设计用于野生卷尾猴面部识别的人工智能模型。

blocks.html_en: Abernethy and Potluri used an open-source software known as YOLO (You Only Look Once) to develop a model to run on a laptop. The researchers trained the model on high-quality GoPro imagery of six wild capuchins interacting with testing platforms in Taboga.

sentences.en: Abernethy and Potluri used an open-source software known as YOLO (You Only Look Once) to develop a model to run on a laptop.
sentences.zh: Abernethy 和 Potluri 使用一种名为 YOLO（You Only Look Once）的开源软件开发了一个在笔记本电脑上运行的模型。

sentences.en: The researchers trained the model on high-quality GoPro imagery of six wild capuchins interacting with testing platforms in Taboga.
sentences.zh: 研究人员利用六只野生卷尾猴与塔博加测试平台互动的高质量 GoPro 图像对模型进行了训练。

blocks.html_en: Emory and Georgia Tech undergraduate students performed the labor-intensive task of digitally placing “bounding boxes” to frame the faces of the monkeys in thousands of still images and videos tagged with their identities.

sentences.en: Emory and Georgia Tech undergraduate students performed the labor-intensive task of digitally placing “bounding boxes” to frame the faces of the monkeys in thousands of still images and videos tagged with their identities.
sentences.zh: 埃默里大学和佐治亚理工学院的本科生执行了一项劳动密集型任务，即以数字方式放置“边界框”，将猴子的脸部框入数千张标有其身份的静态图像和视频中。

blocks.html_en: The result was a facial-recognition system that could identify these six capuchins with 97% accuracy from static images, video and live footage in the field.

sentences.en: The result was a facial-recognition system that could identify these six capuchins with 97% accuracy from static images, video and live footage in the field.
sentences.zh: 其成果是一个面部识别系统，可以从现场的静态图像、视频和实时镜头中以 97% 的准确度识别这六只卷尾猴。

blocks.html_en: Sánchez Vargas, who joined Emory as a graduate student in 2023, took on the next phase of the AI project: figuring out how to integrate the facial-recognition model into a field-friendly, scalable computer interface that could present tasks to interacting capuchins and dispense food rewards.

sentences.en: Sánchez Vargas, who joined Emory as a graduate student in 2023, took on the next phase of the AI project: figuring out how to integrate the facial-recognition model into a field-friendly, scalable computer interface that could present tasks to interacting capuchins and dispense food rewards.
sentences.zh: 桑切斯·瓦尔加斯 (Sánchez Vargas) 于 2023 年作为研究生加入埃默里大学，承担了人工智能项目的下一阶段：研究如何将面部识别模型集成到现场友好的、可扩展的计算机界面中，该界面可以向交互的卷尾猴呈现任务并分发食物奖励。

blocks.html_en: “The model was great at identifying six monkeys, but there are 100 capuchins at the Costa Rica field site,” he says. “And we didn’t have high quality video of all of these individuals, which is needed to train the model.”

sentences.en: “The model was great at identifying six monkeys, but there are 100 capuchins at the Costa Rica field site,” he says.
sentences.zh: “该模型非常适合识别 6 只猴子，但哥斯达黎加现场有 100 只卷尾猴，”他说。

sentences.en: “And we didn’t have high quality video of all of these individuals, which is needed to train the model.”
sentences.zh: “而且我们没有训练模型所需的所有这些人的高质量视频。”

blocks.html_en: Sánchez Vargas’ undergraduate degrees are in evolutionary biology and psychology. He is not an expert computer coder, but he dove into the challenge, using Python programming language to simplify and change the parameters of the original facial-recognition model.

sentences.en: Sánchez Vargas’ undergraduate degrees are in evolutionary biology and psychology.
sentences.zh: 桑切斯·巴尔加斯的本科学位是进化生物学和心理学。

sentences.en: He is not an expert computer coder, but he dove into the challenge, using Python programming language to simplify and change the parameters of the original facial-recognition model.
sentences.zh: 他不是一名计算机编码专家，但他一头扎进了挑战，使用Python编程语言来简化和改变原始面部识别模型的参数。

blocks.html_en: “I essentially dumbed it down,” he says, so that instead of classifying individual capuchin faces, the system recognized any capuchin monkey — and only capuchins.

sentences.en: “I essentially dumbed it down,” he says, so that instead of classifying individual capuchin faces, the system recognized any capuchin monkey — and only capuchins.
sentences.zh: “我基本上把它简化了，”他说，这样系统就不再对单个卷尾猴的面孔进行分类，而是识别任何卷尾猴——而且只识别卷尾猴。

blocks.html_en: The idea, he explains, was to enable the system to trigger a webcam to record video whenever a capuchin approached a computer touchscreen, rapidly generating a larger, more up-to-date dataset of faces from the interacting monkeys. The resulting videos could then be used to keep training the facial-recognition model, expanding its face-recognition repertoire.

sentences.en: The idea, he explains, was to enable the system to trigger a webcam to record video whenever a capuchin approached a computer touchscreen, rapidly generating a larger, more up-to-date dataset of faces from the interacting monkeys.
sentences.zh: 他解释说，这个想法是让系统在卷尾猴接近计算机触摸屏时触发网络摄像头录制视频，从而快速生成来自互动猴子的更大、更新的面部数据集。

sentences.en: The resulting videos could then be used to keep training the facial-recognition model, expanding its face-recognition repertoire.
sentences.zh: 然后，生成的视频可用于继续训练面部识别模型，扩展其面部识别功能。

blocks.html_en: A second Python script Sánchez Vargas developed uses a program called “pygame” to facilitate interactive stimuli for use in games or cognitive testing. The researchers created a simple stimulus to habituate the monkeys to the system: a blue square covering the computer touchscreen that records when a capuchin touches it. At the monkey’s touch, the script signals a motor circuit to dispense a food reward.

sentences.zh: Sánchez Vargas 开发的第二个 Python 脚本使用名为“pygame”的程序来促进游戏或认知测试中使用的交互式刺激。

sentences.en: The researchers created a simple stimulus to habituate the monkeys to the system: a blue square covering the computer touchscreen that records when a capuchin touches it.
sentences.zh: 研究人员创造了一个简单的刺激来让猴子习惯该系统：覆盖计算机触摸屏的蓝色方块，记录卷尾猴触摸它的时间。

sentences.en: At the monkey’s touch, the script signals a motor circuit to dispense a food reward.
sentences.zh: 当猴子触摸时，脚本会向运动电路发出信号，发出食物奖励。

blocks.html_en: The two Python scripts are integrated to run simultaneously on a Raspberry Pi, a tiny computer about half the size of an iPhone. The entire system can run for eight hours on a lightweight battery pack before it needs recharging.

sentences.en: The two Python scripts are integrated to run simultaneously on a Raspberry Pi, a tiny computer about half the size of an iPhone.
sentences.zh: 这两个 Python 脚本集成在一起，可在 Raspberry Pi 上同时运行，Raspberry Pi 是一台只有 iPhone 一半大小的微型计算机。

sentences.en: The entire system can run for eight hours on a lightweight battery pack before it needs recharging.
sentences.zh: 整个系统可以使用轻型电池组运行八个小时，然后才需要充电。

blocks.html_en: “It was important to us that our technology be both low cost and ecologically friendly,” Sánchez Vargas says.

sentences.en: “It was important to us that our technology be both low cost and ecologically friendly,” Sánchez Vargas says.
sentences.zh: “对我们来说，重要的是我们的技术既要低成本又要环保，”Sánchez Vargas 说。

blocks.html_en: The two researchers put together a wooden box, only about 20 inches tall, to house the system’s components: a webcam, a computer touchscreen, the Raspberry Pi, the food dispenser and a rotary motor to power the dispenser.

sentences.en: The two researchers put together a wooden box, only about 20 inches tall, to house the system’s components: a webcam, a computer touchscreen, the Raspberry Pi, the food dispenser and a rotary motor to power the dispenser.

blocks.html_en: “It was a lot of work but also a lot of fun,” Sánchez Vargas says. “One of the best parts of working in animal cognition is getting creative, trying to put yourself into the mind of the animal you’re studying, so you can develop a good way to engage them in experiments.”

sentences.en: “It was a lot of work but also a lot of fun,” Sánchez Vargas says.
sentences.zh: “工作量很大，但也很有趣，”桑切斯·巴尔加斯说。

sentences.en: “One of the best parts of working in animal cognition is getting creative, trying to put yourself into the mind of the animal you’re studying, so you can develop a good way to engage them in experiments.”
sentences.zh: “动物认知研究中最好的部分之一就是发挥创造力，尝试将自己置于所研究动物的思维中，这样你就可以找到一种让它们参与实验的好方法。”

blocks.html_en: The third day, however, a large male capuchin named Trompudo, which means “big snout,” could not resist the scent of banana.

sentences.en: The third day, however, a large male capuchin named Trompudo, which means “big snout,” could not resist the scent of banana.
sentences.zh: 然而，到了第三天，一只名叫 Trompudo（意思是“大鼻子”）的大型雄性卷尾猴无法抗拒香蕉的气味。

blocks.html_en: “He climbs on the box and starts slapping the back of it,” Sánchez Vargas recalls. “Finally, he slaps the touchscreen and a banana slice pops out.”

sentences.en: “He climbs on the box and starts slapping the back of it,” Sánchez Vargas recalls.

sentences.en: “Finally, he slaps the touchscreen and a banana slice pops out.”
sentences.zh: “最后，他敲击触摸屏，一片香蕉片弹出来。”

blocks.html_en: Trompudo gobbled up the food then put his hand on the screen again. Another banana slice popped out.

sentences.en: Trompudo gobbled up the food then put his hand on the screen again.

content_html_zh:
“这个项目建立在弗兰斯·德瓦尔的遗产之上，”该论文的第一作者、埃默里大学人类学博士生费德里科·桑切斯·瓦尔加斯说。

德瓦尔作为埃默里大学猿与人类进化高级研究中心主任，开创了动物认知研究，同时还撰写了畅销书，帮助普及了该领域。 他于 2024 年去世。

桑切斯·巴尔加斯说，除了基于实验室的行为实验外，德瓦尔“还为我们提供了灵长类动物生活的亲密、美丽的肖像，并将它们视为个体”。 “我们的人工智能方法使我们能够通过实地观察更深入地了解我们已经拥有数据的个人。 我们现在可以对它们进行自动化认知测试并量化结果。 这是了解人物背后思想的一种方式。 研究自然环境中的个体，他们的生活经历存在大量差异，让我们了解环境影响如何塑造他们。”

该论文的共同作者包括佐治亚理工学院计算机科学副教授 Jacob Abernethy； Sai Rakshith Potluri，前佐治亚理工学院研究生研究助理，现任西雅图 ExtraHop 的软件工程师。

这份开源论文包括为该系统开发的计算机编码指南，以及构建低技术、低成本现场研究平台并将所有组件集成到闭环管道中的蓝图。 作者希望其他科学家能够调整他们的人工智能方法，生成涵盖生活在各种环境中的不同野生灵长类动物物种的认知数据。

贝尼特斯的工作处于人类学、心理学和进化生物学的交叉点。 她研究猴子的合作和其他社会行为，包括实验室圈养的簇绒卷尾猴和哥斯达黎加东北部塔博加森林保护区的野生白面卷尾猴。 她是 Capuchinos de Taboga 的联合主任，该项目于 2017 年与哥斯达黎加国立技术大学合作启动。

实验室中的动物实验可以受到严格控制。 然而，由于动物没有在自然环境中相互作用，因此结果可能会有所偏差。 野外动物行为实验提供了有效的社会和生态背景，但它们的设计和控制具有挑战性。

“我正在努力弥合这一差距，”贝尼特斯说。

她决定研究人工智能实现这一目标的潜力。

埃默里大学 AI.Humanity 项目的种子基金启动了贝尼特斯和阿伯内西之间的合作，设计用于野生卷尾猴面部识别的人工智能模型。

Abernethy 和 Potluri 使用一种名为 YOLO（You Only Look Once）的开源软件开发了一个在笔记本电脑上运行的模型。 研究人员利用六只野生卷尾猴与塔博加测试平台互动的高质量 GoPro 图像对模型进行了训练。

埃默里大学和佐治亚理工学院的本科生执行了一项劳动密集型任务，即以数字方式放置“边界框”，将猴子的脸部框入数千张标有其身份的静态图像和视频中。

其成果是一个面部识别系统，可以从现场的静态图像、视频和实时镜头中以 97% 的准确度识别这六只卷尾猴。

桑切斯·瓦尔加斯 (Sánchez Vargas) 于 2023 年作为研究生加入埃默里大学，承担了人工智能项目的下一阶段：研究如何将面部识别模型集成到现场友好的、可扩展的计算机界面中，该界面可以向交互的卷尾猴呈现任务并分发食物奖励。

“该模型非常适合识别 6 只猴子，但哥斯达黎加现场有 100 只卷尾猴，”他说。 “而且我们没有训练模型所需的所有这些人的高质量视频。”

桑切斯·巴尔加斯的本科学位是进化生物学和心理学。 他不是一名计算机编码专家，但他一头扎进了挑战，使用Python编程语言来简化和改变原始面部识别模型的参数。

“我基本上把它简化了，”他说，这样系统就不再对单个卷尾猴的面孔进行分类，而是识别任何卷尾猴——而且只识别卷尾猴。

他解释说，这个想法是让系统在卷尾猴接近计算机触摸屏时触发网络摄像头录制视频，从而快速生成来自互动猴子的更大、更新的面部数据集。 然后，生成的视频可用于继续训练面部识别模型，扩展其面部识别功能。

Sánchez Vargas 开发的第二个 Python 脚本使用名为“pygame”的程序来促进游戏或认知测试中使用的交互式刺激。 研究人员创造了一个简单的刺激来让猴子习惯该系统：覆盖计算机触摸屏的蓝色方块，记录卷尾猴触摸它的时间。 当猴子触摸时，脚本会向运动电路发出信号，发出食物奖励。

这两个 Python 脚本集成在一起，可在 Raspberry Pi 上同时运行，Raspberry Pi 是一台只有 iPhone 一半大小的微型计算机。 整个系统可以使用轻型电池组运行八个小时，然后才需要充电。

“对我们来说，重要的是我们的技术既要低成本又要环保，”Sánchez Vargas 说。

下一个挑战是创建一个防野生动物、防风雨的平台来容纳系统的所有组件。

“我们在我的车库里建造了它，”贝尼特斯说。

她和桑切斯·巴尔加斯从家得宝购买了松木板、甲板密封剂、橡胶绝缘条和塑料管道。

“一个帮助我们的人问，‘你们正在从事的项目是什么？’”贝尼特斯说。 “我们没有深入探讨；解释起来有点复杂。”

Emory TechLab 帮助 Sánchez Vargas 创建了 3D 打印塑料食品分配器。

两位研究人员组装了一个仅约 20 英寸高的木箱，用来容纳系统的组件：网络摄像头、电脑触摸屏、Raspberry Pi、食物分配器和为分配器供电的旋转电机。

“工作量很大，但也很有趣，”桑切斯·巴尔加斯说。 “动物认知研究中最好的部分之一就是发挥创造力，尝试将自己置于所研究动物的思维中，这样你就可以找到一种让它们参与实验的好方法。”

最后，是时候在现场测试他们的创作了。

到达哥斯达黎加 Capuchinos de Toboga 工厂后，桑切斯·巴尔加斯 (Sánchez Vargas) 记得在最后一刻感到有些紧张。 原型会按预期发挥作用吗？

“我们必须在凌晨四点起床，”他说，“沿着这条崎岖不平的道路行驶很长一段路才能到达研究地点。”

该团队将 CapuchinAI 盒子固定在一个平台上，在食品分配器中装入干森林香蕉片，然后在附近等待。

“我们这样做的头几天，没有卷尾猴来过，”桑切斯·巴尔加斯说。 “我开始担心了。”

然而，到了第三天，一只名叫 Trompudo（意思是“大鼻子”）的大型雄性卷尾猴无法抗拒香蕉的气味。

“他爬上箱子，开始拍打箱子的背面，”桑切斯·巴尔加斯回忆道。 “最后，他敲击触摸屏，一片香蕉片弹出来。”

特龙普多狼吞虎咽地吃完食物，然后再次把手放在屏幕上。 又一块香蕉片弹出来。

“你几乎可以看到他意识到，‘啊，这就是你必须做的，触摸屏幕！’”桑切斯·巴尔加斯说。 “看到一个人如此快速地学习东西真是太神奇了。”
